attribution_limitations: The place of death is described two ways: she passed away at home surrounded by her family, and the Fig. 3 caption says she died on day 99 of hospitalization. Both sides are quarantined; the death on day 99 itself is agreed.
The text places the γGTP value of 373 U/L at 17 days after the first T-DXd cycle, while the Fig. 3 pixels print 373 at the Day 18 point; the pixel value is kept in visual.json only.
The IgG4 value of 8 mg/dL lies below the printed reference interval 11 to 121 mg/dL, yet the source groups IgG4 among values within normal limits.
The antimitochondrial M2 antibody value is printed in U/mL while its reference interval is printed in U/dL.
The day 49 paragraph says drug-induced cholangitis was diagnosed, while the abstract and conclusion say suspected drug-induced SC and that a definitive diagnosis could not be established.
Anorexia appears only inside the sentence about a possible cause of obstruction.
The MRI phobia limited diagnostic evaluation, but the source does not state that an MRI was ordered or not performed.
The agent of each antibiotic course is not named, and the abstract antibiotic sentence follows the 17-day cholangitis statement without a day number.

The source cannot attribute the cholangitis to a single agent among paclitaxel, bevacizumab and T-DXd, and the onset is stated as 17 days, 2 weeks after the first T-DXd dose and 2 months after four cycles of paclitaxel with bevacizumab.

The Fig. 3 chart prints 82/52 at the right end of the AST and ALT lines with no units or reference range, while the caption says hepatic transaminase levels remained within normal limits throughout treatment; the pixel values stay in visual.json and are not classified against outside ranges.

evidence.quote:
Fig. 1.
CT imaging. a CT imaging performed 17 days after the first cycle of T-DXd. Dilation of the intrahepatic bile ducts is observed, with no definite site of obstruction identified (arrow). b CT imaging performed 49 days after the first cycle of T-DXd. Mild dilation of the common bile duct wall is observed. A beaded appearance, characterized by alternating strictures and dilations with a periportal collar sign, is noted diffusely involving bile ducts in both hepatic lobes (arrows).

Fig. 2.
Pathological findings. During ERCP, biopsies were obtained from four sites in the papilla, one site at the confluence of the right and left hepatic ducts, and one site from the distal bile duct. a Stromal fibrosis with infiltration of inflammatory cells, including neutrophils. No evidence of neoplastic lesions is detected. Obliterative phlebitis is not clearly identified. b IgG4+ cells are scarce. ERCP, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography.

Fig. 3.
Trends in laboratory findings. At the time of the first administration of T-DXd, inflammatory markers and hepatobiliary enzymes were within normal ranges. On day 17, elevated CRP levels prompted antibiotic therapy initiation. Although CRP levels decreased, γGTP levels continued to rise. On day 49, when symptoms reappeared, elevations in CRP, γGTP, and TB were observed. Despite additional antibiotic administration and placement of an ERBD tube, CRP decreased, while γGTP and TB remained elevated. Hepatic transaminase levels remained within normal limits throughout treatment. Laboratory tests were not performed following the transition to home-based care. The patient died on day 99 of hospitalization. TB, total bilirubin; ERBD, endoscopic retrograde biliary drainage.
